summary: postinstall fetches and executes opaque binary from hardcoded bare-IP endpoint with TLS verification disabled
details: The npm postinstall lifecycle script downloads an `onecode` platform tarball from a hardcoded bare-IPv4 URL (https://218.90.133.98:4443/onecode_tgz/onecode-<ver>/onecode-linux-x64-<ver>.tgz), extracts it into node_modules, hardlinks the resulting binary into bin/.onecode with mode 0755, and follows HTTP 301/302 redirects. The HTTPS request is issued with `rejectUnauthorized: false`, disabling certificate validation so any TLS peer on that IP or on-path is accepted. No hash, signature, or other integrity check is applied to the fetched bytes. The destination is a bare IPv4 with no relationship to the package scope (@onescience) or any publisher domain, and the fetched content is an opaque executable that becomes the package's CLI on `npm install`. The combination — non-publisher bare-IP source, TLS verification disabled, unpinned mutable payload, install-time chmod+wire-up as CLI — provides full-host code execution to whoever controls that IP or can position on-path to the connection.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
